key_insight: A lightweight transformer-based inpainting model fills missing textures in real-time 3D streaming from sparse multi-camera rigs, producing cross-view and temporal consistency without needing dense capture.
problem_solved: Addresses visual holes and inconsistent surface textures that occur when reconstructing and streaming 3D scenes from only a few cameras under real-time constraints.
method: Use a transformer to aggregate multi-view image tokens and infer plausible content for missing/occluded texture regions.
Condition the network on camera poses and/or geometric cues so predicted fills align across views and map correctly to 3D surfaces.
Design a latency-optimized architecture and training losses (e.g., perceptual, view-consistency, temporal) to maintain real-time performance and stable streaming.
impact: Enables higher visual fidelity for AR/VR and live 3D telepresence with fewer cameras and strict latency budgets, reducing hardware cost while improving user immersion and reducing artifacts.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: sparse multi-camera inputs → transformer inpainting module (pose/depth conditioning) → textured 3D output

paper_title: Transformer-Based Inpainting for Real-Time 3D Streaming in Sparse Multi-Camera Setups
paper_authors: Leif Van Holland, Domenic Zingsheim, Mana Takhsha, Hannah Dröge, Patrick Stotko
